text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Communists expected to take part in the new government whose composition will be announced today.
-- French industries' investments abroad rose by 84.2 percent in 1996.
-- CFDT union leader Nicole Notat in favour of opening capital of France Telecom.
-- Germany's Dresdner Bank does not rule out tightening ties with BNP.
-- SNCF railway operator to ask for two to three billion francs in compensation from public works contractors found guilty in court of distorting competition.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Unions to put pressure on new government on social issues.
-- Paris bourse picks up, partly due to steady interest rates.
-- New government may consider cutting credits to nuclear missile programs.
-- Generale des Eaux telecoms unit Cegetel's managing director Philippe Germond says in an interview interconnection prices favour operators who invest in infrastructure.
L'AGEFI
-- Non-resident investors cautious about investing in Paris.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Labour tensions in auto sector to test new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
-- Paris stock exchange registered record activity in May.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Former National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin launches campaign to replace former Prime Minister Alain Juppe as head of Gaullist party RPR.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- CFDT union leader Nicole Notat is open to France Telecom partial share sale since the state would retain a stake allowing it to protect public service.
